\title{Test-Time Refinement Moves Intelligibility Six Times More Than\\
Identity in Masked-Diffusion TTS}
\author{Anonymous authors\\Paper under double-blind review}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
A diffusion language model buys sequential computation twice: depth, paid once in
parameters, and denoising steps, rented per utterance at serve time. We ask whether the
rented kind helps every capability equally. We train an iso-parameter width--depth grid
of \Nconfigs\ masked-diffusion codec TTS models (\Nseeds\ seeds, 20--125\,M non-embedding
parameters) and sweep the refinement budget $T$ at inference only, giving a \Nsurface-point
$(w,d,T)$ surface per metric from \Nruns\ trained models. Fitting
$\mathrm{err}=E+Aw^{-\alpha}+Bd^{-\beta}+CT^{-\tau}$ pre-registered, test-time scaling is
metric-selective: $\Delta\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{WER}}-\tau_{\mathrm{SIM}}=\Ndtau$, 95\%
run-level bootstrap CI \Ndtauci, excluding zero. The effect that carries practical weight
is one of \emph{magnitude}: over $\tc{T}{=}1\to16$ refinement moves \NabsWERgain\ absolute
WER (a \NwerratioT\ reduction) against \NabsSIMgain\ absolute speaker-similarity error
(\NsimratioT), a \NmagAsym\ asymmetry. It is not a difference in convergence \emph{rate}:
on each metric's own normalised curve the fraction of total gain realised by $\tc{T}{=}8$ is
\NfracTeightWER\% for WER and \NfracTeightSIM\% for identity, identity marginally later.
The selectivity persists across a \NmaxNfour\,M four-budget replication,
$\Delta\tau=\Ndtaufour$, CI \Ndtaufourci. The asymmetry is less a limit on what inference can
buy than on what \emph{refinement} can buy: at matched NFE, best-of-$K$ search
moves speaker similarity by \NsearchDelta\ (CI \NsearchCI) against refinement at
$\tc{T}{=}64$, or \NsearchVsDefault\ against the deployable $\tc{T}{=}16$ default,
where refinement moves it least. Depth and steps are \emph{not} interchangeable:
the substitution form $B(d\,T^{\kappa})^{-\beta}$ is worse than the separable form by
$\Delta\mathrm{AICc}=+\NaiccSSWER$.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
A diffusion language model can buy sequential computation twice. It \emph{owns} depth:
$d$ transformer blocks, paid once in parameters and then on every forward pass forever.
It \emph{rents} refinement steps: $T$ denoising passes over the same sequence, paid per
utterance and adjustable at serve time. An autoregressive model has only the first lever;
its serial cost per token is fixed by the architecture the moment training ends. If rented
serial compute substitutes for owned serial compute, a deployment can trade parameters for
steps after the fact --- but only for the capabilities that steps actually improve.

Zero-shot text-to-speech is a clean probe: intelligibility is compositional (the right
phonetic content in the right order, read out by word error rate) while speaker identity is
representational (timbre carried from a short prompt, read out by SIM-o). The two need not
respond to the same knob.

We train one iso-parameter width--depth grid of masked-diffusion codec language models and
then sweep $T$ at inference only, which yields a full $(w, d, T)$ response surface per
metric at zero additional training cost. Two claims were pre-registered before any run.
\textbf{H-D2}: refinement steps improve intelligibility more than identity, i.e.\ test-time
scaling is metric-selective. \textbf{H-D3}: for intelligibility, steps and depth exchange at
a measurable rate $\kappa$ --- how many step-doublings buy one depth-doubling.

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:models}
\begin{aligned}
\text{separable:}\quad &\mathrm{err}_m(w,d,T) = E_m + A_m w^{-\alpha_m} + B_m d^{-\beta_m} + C_m T^{-\tau_m}\\[-1pt]
\text{substitution:}\quad &\mathrm{err}_m(w,d,T) = E_m + A_m w^{-\alpha_m} + B_m \big(d\,T^{\kappa_m}\big)^{-\beta_m}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

The first answer is yes and quantitative: $\Delta\tau = \Ndtau$, run-level bootstrap CI
\Ndtauci. The second is a clean no --- the substitution form is decisively \emph{worse} than
the separable one ($\Delta\mathrm{AICc}=+\NaiccSSWER$ for WER, $+\NaiccSSSIM$ for SIM-o) and
$\kappa$ runs to its bound, so no finite depth--step exchange rate describes this regime.
Extra inference compute is a targeted instrument, not a substitute for architecture.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em, itemsep=1pt, topsep=2pt]
\item[\cnum{1}] The first per-metric $(\wc{w}, \dc{d}, \tc{T})$ scaling surface for speech
generation: \Nsurface\ points per metric from \Nruns\ models.
\item[\cnum{2}] $\Delta\tau = \Ndtau$, CI \Ndtauci\ --- steps are metric-selective --- with
depth--step substitution reported as a \emph{negative} AICc result ($+\NaiccSSWER$) and
$\kappa$ as unidentified.
\item[\cnum{3}] An identity ledger against a measured codec ceiling: what moves speaker
similarity when refinement does not --- training compute and test-time selection.
\end{itemize}

\section{Related work}
Masked diffusion language models are trained at scale \citep{llada,mdlm,d3pm}, but their
scaling is reported against a single likelihood-shaped objective, so a per-capability
question cannot arise. The masked-generative recipes that made codec-token TTS practical
\citep{soundstorm,maskgit,maskgct} fixed a step budget by engineering judgement and report a
single operating point; none maps error against steps as a law. Autoregressive codec TTS
\citep{valle} reports scaling in total parameters only \citep{llasa}, which separates neither
width from depth nor either from steps, as is true of classical scaling work
\citep{kaplan,chinchilla}. Test-time scaling is well studied in reasoning \citep{testtime},
where the payoff is one correctness metric; whether extra inference compute helps different
capabilities \emph{differently} is, to our knowledge, untested in generative speech.

\section{Method}
\paragraph{Backbone and objective.}
A bidirectional (non-causal) pre-LN transformer over Mimi \citep{moshi} codec tokens at 12.5\,Hz with the
first 8 residual codebooks (2048 entries each, plus MASK and PAD). \wc{Width $w$}, \dc{depth $d$}, head dimension 64, GELU MLP ratio 4, RMSNorm, RoPE, no weight tying, so the non-embedding
parameter count is $N = 12\,d\,w^{2}$. One embedding table per codebook is summed at the
input and one linear head per codebook reads out. Training is SoundStorm-style \citep{soundstorm}
coarse-to-fine masking: per example a level $l \sim \mathcal{U}\{1..8\}$ and a ratio
$t \sim \mathcal{U}(0,1]$; levels below $l$ stay visible, level $l$ is masked i.i.d.\ with
probability $t$, levels above $l$ are entirely MASK; the loss is cross-entropy on the masked
cells of level $l$ only. A phoneme prefix and a 3-second prompt of codec tokens are always
visible; there is no speaker encoder, so the backbone is the only identity pathway, and no
classifier-free guidance, which would confound the step axis. The target length is fixed before generation from the text length and a
corpus character rate ($\Nsecperchar$\,s/char).

\paragraph{Frozen sampler.}
MaskGIT-style confidence decoding \citep{maskgit}, level by level, with exactly \tc{$T$
refinement steps per level}, so NFE $= 8T$: a cosine schedule sets how many cells remain
masked after each step, tokens are drawn at temperature 1.0, and confidences are
log-probabilities plus Gumbel noise annealed $1 \to 0$; committed cells stay committed. The
sampler is identical for every config, seed and $T$, and generation noise is keyed so that
$T$ is the only difference between surface points of one run. We verify $T$ reaches the
sampler before computing any metric: $T{=}1$ and $T{=}16$ must differ on $>$20\% of cells.

\paragraph{Design and statistics.}
$\Nconfigs$ configs span three iso-$N$ budgets $\times$ five aspect ratios, each trained at
$\Nseeds$ seeds for 30{,}000 steps at effective batch 256 with $\mu$P \citep{mup} (base width
256, base LR $\Nbaselr$; transfer verified by five-point LR sweeps). $T \in \{\NTgrid\}$ is
swept at evaluation only, giving $\Nsurface$ surface points per metric from $\Nruns$ models.
Metrics: WER (Whisper-large-v3 \citep{whisper}, greedy), SIM-o (WavLM-large \citep{wavlm}
against the \emph{original} prompt waveform, following \citet{seedtts}), a frozen
degenerate-output rule, and UTMOS \citep{utmos}.
Error transforms are $\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{WER}} = \mathrm{WER}$ and
$\mathrm{err}_{\mathrm{SIM}} = 1 - \text{SIM-o}$, computed over all items including
degenerates. Both forms of Eq.~\eqref{eq:models} are fitted by weighted non-linear least
squares with 32 multi-starts; $\Delta\tau = \tau_{\mathrm{WER}} - \tau_{\mathrm{SIM}}$,
$\kappa$, and $\Delta\rho = \alpha_{\mathrm{SIM}}/\beta_{\mathrm{SIM}} -
\alpha_{\mathrm{WER}}/\beta_{\mathrm{WER}}$ carry percentile confidence intervals from a
bootstrap that resamples at the \emph{run} level --- the five $T$-points of one run share a
trained model, so resampling surface points would understate their correlation --- with
$\Nbootreps$ replicates recomputing every $T$ point.

\section{Results}
\paragraph{Steps are metric-selective (H-D2, supported).}
Fitted on all \Nsurface\ surface points, the step exponent is $\tau_{\mathrm{WER}} =
\Ntauwer$ (CI \Ntauwerci) against $\tau_{\mathrm{SIM}} = \Ntausim$ (CI \Ntausimci), so
$\Delta\tau = \Ndtau$ with CI \Ndtauci, excluding zero. The raw surface shows it without any model: over the grid, $\tc{T}{=}1 \to \tc{T}{=}16$
takes WER from \Nwertone\% to \Nwertsixteen\% (a factor of \NwerratioT\ on the error scale)
while SIM-o moves only \Nsimtone\ $\to$ \Nsimtsixteen\ (\NsimratioT\ on $1-\text{SIM-o}$),
an absolute-error asymmetry of \NmagAsym. The selectivity is not an artefact of scale,
training compute, or the metric stack: a fourth budget (\NmaxNfour\,M, ten further runs)
gives $\Delta\tau = \Ndtaufour$, CI \Ndtaufourci; retraining three configurations $3\times$
longer gives \Ndtaunineok, CI \Ndtaunineokci; and a different ASR or unbounded
log-amplitudes move it to \Ndtauasr\ and \Ndtaulogamp. Extending $T$ to 64 shows WER still
falling past the grid edge (\NwerTsixteenExt\ $\to$ \NwerTsixtyfour), so the $\tc{T}{=}16$
value was a lower bound. The power gate \Ngfour\ in all three budgets before these tests ran.

\paragraph{Depth and steps do not substitute (H-D3, not supported).}
The pre-registered substitution form collapses: $\Delta\mathrm{AICc}
(M_{\mathrm{sub}}-M_{\mathrm{sep}}) = +\NaiccSSWER$ for WER and $+\NaiccSSSIM$ for SIM-o
where the hypothesis required $\le +4$, and $\kappa$ sits on its bound for both metrics, so
we quote none. The fits show why: $T$ enters as an additive term decaying to a floor, while
depth moves the floor itself, and one factor $d\,T^{\kappa}$ cannot fit both orderings.

\paragraph{Shape matters, but the anisotropy ratio is not identified (H-D1, not supported).}
At $\tc{T}{=}16$ the two-axis model beats the $N$-only model for both metrics
($\Delta\mathrm{AICc} = \NaiccFNWER$ / $\NaiccFNSIM$ against a $-4$ threshold), so error is
not a function of parameter count alone. The \emph{direction} of the anisotropy we cannot
claim: $\Delta\rho = \Ndrho$, CI \Ndrhoci\ spanning zero, because the width amplitude
saturates its pre-registered bound in every fit, leaving only $A\,w^{-\alpha}$ identified.
\dc{Depth} is identified and separates the capabilities sharply
($\beta_{\mathrm{WER}} = \NbetaBWER$ versus $\beta_{\mathrm{SIM}} = \NbetaBSIM$): moving from
the shallowest shape to the best depth is worth \NdepthgainA, \NdepthgainB\ and
\NdepthgainC\ WER points across the three budgets, while SIM-o varies by under
\NsimspreadTsixteen. The depth optimum is interior only in the smallest budget; in the two
larger ones the argmin sits at the deepest shape tested, so we claim no $d^{*}(N)$ trend.

\paragraph{Extrapolation and reliability.}
Fitting the two smaller budgets to predict the largest gives MAPE \NmapeSIM\% for SIM-o
(versus \NmapeNSIM\% $N$-only), inside the 15\% asked for; WER does not extrapolate
(\NmapeWER\% versus \NmapeNWER\%). Degeneracy falls monotonically with $T$, \Ndegentone\% to
\Ndegentsixteen\%: most of what $T{=}1$ costs is outright failure.

\paragraph{Serving corollary.}
Measured at batch 1, $c_{\mathrm{layer}}$ is flat in width (\Nclayerrange\ ms per layer for
$w \in [256, 1152]$): the device is launch-bound, so serial latency is
$8\,T\,d\,c_{\mathrm{layer}}$ and width is free, leaving a latency budget to constrain only
the product $T\,d$. Our data do not resolve how to split it --- the pre-registered
depth-before-steps rule held at 5.9\% of 40 budgets against an 80\% bar, and $T$ is censored
at 16 --- so we claim no directional allocation rule.

\paragraph{What buys identity, measured against a ceiling.}
If refinement is an intelligibility knob, what moves identity? We measure the candidates on
one scale against a bound: a codec round-trip of ground-truth audio scores \NsimRoundtrip,
leaving \NheadroomSim\ of headroom above our best system. The largest lever is
\emph{training compute} (30k${\to}$90k steps, \NtrainGainSim, CI \NtrainGainCI\ over
\NtrainGainRuns\ runs; a further doubling adds \NtrainDouble). Next is \emph{test-time
search}: at matched NFE ($8T$ per candidate), best-of-$K$ sampling with candidates chosen by
one speaker encoder and scored by a second, independently gated one (\S\,Limitations)
improves similarity by \NsearchDelta\ (CI \NsearchCI, \NsearchWin\,\% of items) over
refinement at $\tc{T}{=}64$, or \NsearchVsDefault\ over the deployable $\tc{T}{=}16$ default
for \NsearchWERcost\ WER --- while refinement stays the better spend for intelligibility
(WER \NrefineWER\ versus \NsearchWER). The gain is selection, not sampling: an arbitrary
candidate scores \NrandomPick\ regardless of $K$. It persists at \NsearchMaxN\,M
non-embedding parameters (\NsearchD) and, on three runs, at $3\times$ training compute
(\NsearchNinetyk). Further behind sit a $14\times$ parameter increase (\NparamGainSim) and
training-free speaker-contrastive guidance (\NguideGainSim, for \NguideWER\ WER points --- a
trade), while rate-matched length conditioning (\NrateGainSim) and longer prompts buy
nothing: the best prompt is the 3\,s default seen in training, and beyond it output stays
fluent and speaker-consistent while decoupling from the text. Identity is bought with
training and selection, not with more refinement.

\emph{Where} the passes are spent matters as much as how many: at matched
NFE${}=32$, moving them to the coarsest codebook level changes WER from
\NnfeFineWER\ to \NnfeCoarseWER, at a cost in identity and naturalness
(Appendix~\ref{app:alloc}).

\section{Limitations and outlook}
Our ceiling is \NmaxN\,M non-embedding parameters and 30{,}000 steps, so every model is
under-trained and $T^{*}_{\mathrm{WER}}$ is a lower bound. Part of the identity gap is not
ours to close: a codec round-trip of the target scores \NsimRoundtrip\ against
\NsimRealAudio\ for the original, so \NcodecShare\% of the distance to real speech is lost in
the codec. The search result carries one limitation we
could not close: selector and scorer are both ECAPA-TDNN-family encoders (item-level
$r={\NselCorrRange}$); each passes the ground-truth speaker gate independently and the
selector captures only \NoracleShare\,\% of an oracle's gap where shared bias would predict
nearly all of it, but excluding representational overlap needs a different scorer family, and
matching is on diffusion NFE only. One language, one codec, one corpus, and no
classifier-free guidance. The $\Delta\tau$ interval captures seed variation only; target
length comes from a corpus median; $\Delta\rho$ and $\kappa$ are unidentified.
Cuts taken: \Ncuts; pre-registered outcome class \Noutcome.

before the first run, and every gate is logged with its measured values. The released
artefact holds the harness, all \Nruns\ run records, the \Nsurface-point surface, and the
fitting and bootstrap code. Total cost \Ngpuhours\ GPU-hours.

\section{Refinement-budget allocation across codebook levels}
\label{app:alloc}
Three frozen per-level step schedules at matched total NFE${}=32$ on the \Nbudgetc\ budget
(15 runs, 400 items). Paired item-level bootstrap, \Nbootreps\ replicates, pairing on the
eval item so item difficulty cancels. Coarse spends all passes on codebook level 0, fine on
level 7, uniform splits evenly.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
schedule & WER & SIM-o & UTMOS & degenerate \\
\midrule
coarse \texttt{[25,1,...,1]}  & \NnfeCoarseWER  & \NnfeCoarseSIM  & \NnfeCoarseUT  & \NnfeCoarseDegen\% \\
uniform \texttt{[4,...,4]}    & \NnfeUniformWER & \NnfeUniformSIM & \NnfeUniformUT & \NnfeUniformDegen\% \\
fine \texttt{[1,...,1,25]}    & \NnfeFineWER    & \NnfeFineSIM    & \NnfeFineUT    & \NnfeFineDegen\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Allocation is metric-selective in the same way the step \emph{count} is: coarse
wins WER but loses identity and naturalness against uniform, both with intervals excluding
zero. It is a trade, not a free win.

\paragraph{A significance-based saturation contrast.} Defining saturation as the smallest
$T$ whose paired-bootstrap interval for $\mathrm{err}(T)-\mathrm{err}(64)$ covers zero
gives $T^{*}_{\mathrm{WER}}=32$ against $T^{*}_{\mathrm{SIM}}=16$ on the extended grid.
We report this only here and do not build on it: roughly half the contrast is a precision
artefact, since identity's detection floor is ${\approx}1.8\times$ looser relative to its own
dynamic range than intelligibility's. The raw-scale $T^{*}$ --- 95\% of the
$T{=}16$ \emph{value} --- is not affine-invariant and must never be compared across metrics:
the same 5\% band is 0.67\% of WER's range but 11.96\% of SIM-o's. On the invariant
fraction-of-total-gain definition, $T^{*}=16$ for both metrics.

\section{Fit diagnostics and exploratory analyses}
\label{app:diag}
\textbf{Parameters at bounds.} The width amplitude $A$ saturates the pre-registered
\emph{upper} bound $A \le 10$ in every fit (Part A: 10.000 for both metrics; Part B: 9.999
for WER, 10.000 for SIM-o), so only the product $A\,w^{-\alpha}$ is identified and
$\alpha$ is not; the bound, not the data, is binding, which is a limitation of the
pre-registered parameterisation worth fixing in any follow-up. $\kappa$ reaches its upper
bound in every one of the \Nbootreps\ bootstrap replicates of $M_{\mathrm{sub}}$. The
irreducible term $E$ reaches 0 for WER under $M_{\mathrm{sep}}$. The depth amplitude $B$ is
interior throughout, so $\beta$ is identified.

\textbf{Exploratory: the depth exponent separates the capabilities.}
$\beta_{\mathrm{WER}} = \NbetaBWER$ against $\beta_{\mathrm{SIM}} = \NbetaBSIM$, a factor
of 3.7 --- the asymmetry H-D1 sought, in the parameter the data pin down. Part-B $\rho$
values point the pre-registered way ($\Delta\rho = +0.890$) but inherit the $A$-cap
problem; the pre-registered test is Part A, so this is exploratory only.

\textbf{Weighting.} Points are weighted $1/\mathrm{SE}^2$ with SE taken over seeds, floored
at a quarter of the pooled seed SD so that a chance agreement between two seeds cannot
dominate the fit; the number of floored points is recorded in the released
\texttt{fits.json}.

\textbf{Exploratory (not part of any declared claim).} An unweighted refit of both parts is
released alongside the weighted fit, as is a fit that additionally includes the finished
runs of a stretch third seed. Both reproduce the sign and significance of $\Delta\tau$.

\section*{Use of Generative AI Disclosure}
Generative AI was used as a coding assistant for the experimental harness and for language
refinement of author-written text. The research design, the pre-registered hypotheses and
